workflow.title: Production workflow
workflow.subtitle: Design, version, and publish factory stage paths
workflow.manageStagesSubtitle: Name and configure stages used across every workflow. Locked stages always stay.
workflow.deleteStageConfirm: “{name}” will be removed from every workflow. Orders that already used this stage keep it.
workflow.cannotEditLockedStage: This stage is locked and cannot be edited or deleted.
workflow.cannotRenameLockedStage: The name is locked. You can still change time, photos, and how it is scheduled.
workflow.futureOrdersOnly: This will affect future production orders only.
workflow.beforeInspectionHint: New production stages always feed into Inspection next.
workflow.thenGoesToHint: Production stages always continue into the required finishing path.
workflow.howScheduled: What should the calendar wait for?
workflow.scheduleByWorkersHint: The calendar waits for workers who can do this work.
workflow.scheduleByWorkersNote: Most stages use this. The schedule fills around available people.
workflow.scheduleByResourceHint: Only a few can run at once — a spray booth, CNC, oven, or similar.

workflow.durationHoursHint: Typical time on the floor. Used when planning the calendar.
workflow.requiresInspectionHint: A quality check before the next stage.

workflow.stagesHint: Stages flow top to bottom. Parallel stages run together.

workflow.assignWorkersHint: These workers can be assigned when this stage runs on an order.
workflow.noWorkers: No workers available yet. Create worker users in Admin first.
workflow.productSectionHint: Pick which workflow this product uses when orders are confirmed.
workflow.placementHint: Choose where this stage sits in the path.
workflow.chartPreviewHint: Path preview — same circle map used in production.

workflow.leadsIntoPickHint: Leave empty to keep the usual path. Only stages this one can actually feed are listed.

workflow.disconnectedHint: No links selected — this stage won’t connect until you edit it.
workflow.willBecomeLast: Production stages join Inspection — Delivery stays the locked end.

workflow.discardConfirm: Leave without publishing? Unpublished edits to this workflow will be discarded.

workflow.pickStageFirst: Pick or create a stage name first, then tap Add stage.
workflow.mergeHint: When several stages lead into one, that stage waits until all of them finish.
workflow.emptyFirstStage: Add the first stage to start this production path.
workflow.reconnectExplain: Removing this stage reconnects what ran before it to what came after, so the path stays connected.
workflow.deactivateConfirm: Deactivate this stage? Existing workflows keep it; it won’t appear when adding new stages.
workflow.publishedReadOnly: This published version is read-only. Create a draft to make changes.
workflow.namesHint: Name the stage in every language used on the floor.
workflow.terminalHint: Every workflow ends with Inspection, Packaging, and Delivery. These stages are locked.

workflow.terminalPackagingDesc: Takes the inspected couch and packs it into ship packages.
workflow.terminalDeliveryDesc: Takes Packaging’s packages; after every package is checked onto the truck and load is confirmed, the customer sees the order on the way.
workflow.placementPickRequired: Pick at least one stage for this placement.

setup.title: Production setup
setup.subtitle: Configure workflow, materials, and what each stage uses or produces. New orders only — existing orders keep their snapshot.
setup.newOrdersOnly: Changes apply to new production orders only. Existing orders keep their frozen workflow.
setup.previewEmpty: Save a setup to preview how inventory will move.
setup.previewHint: How materials and pieces move stage by stage after you save.
setup.stageIoCaption: Each stage can take materials and/or semi-finished pieces, and can make a new piece for the next stage.
setup.screenHint: Tap a stage to set what it takes in and what it makes. Materials and components can both apply on the same stage.
setup.stagesHint: Factory order — parallels share a step number. Delivery finishes the flow.
setup.parallelWithSiblings: Runs in parallel with the other stage(s) on this step
setup.bomSharedHint: Product materials list. Choose which materials each stage uses when you open the stage.
setup.takesInHint: Warehouse materials and/or semi-finished pieces from earlier stages.
setup.takeMaterialsHint: Pull materials from the warehouse for this stage.
setup.takeSemiHint: Receive pieces produced upstream (for example carpentry → assembly). Each piece can only be taken once.
setup.makesHint: What this stage hands to the next station — or nothing if it only prepares or inspects.
setup.makeNothing: Does not produce a stocked piece
setup.makeNothingHint: Prep work that does not create a new inventory item. Packaging always makes finished goods.
setup.makeSemiHint: Creates a component waiting for the next production stage.
setup.makeFinishedHint: Creates the sellable finished good for this product.
setup.inspectionIoCaption: Confirms the couch is good to package — does not create stock.
setup.packagingIoCaption: Takes the inspected couch and packs it into ship packages.
setup.deliveryIoCaption: Takes Packaging’s packages; after every package is checked onto the truck and load is confirmed, the customer sees the order on the way.
setup.inspectionTakesInHint: Assign the upstream semi-finished kit this inspection confirms.
setup.packagingTakesInHint: Take the inspected couch kit from upstream production.
setup.deliveryTakesInHint: Packages come from Packaging — the driver checks them off on the load sheet.
setup.deliveryPackagesMissing: Set package count on Packaging first
setup.deliveryPackagesLoadHint: Checking every package off and confirming load tells the customer the order is on the way.
setup.inspectionMakesHint: Inspection is a QC gate only — no stocked output.
setup.packagingMakesHint: Packaging always makes the finished product and ship packages.
setup.deliveryMakesHint: Delivery does not create stock — packages are checked onto the truck.
setup.inspectionConfirmOnlyHint: Pass or fail the kit; Packaging creates finished goods next.
setup.deliveryConfirmOnlyHint: Driver checks Packaging’s packages onto the truck, then Confirm load.
setup.kitNameHint: One kit for the next stage — pieces below are the parts inside it.
setup.piecesHint: Add every physical piece the next stage should receive.
setup.finishedUsesProductName: Uses the product name — no separate label needed.
setup.packPiecesHint: How many physical packages ship together (for example a bed in 4 packages).
setup.packPieceNamesHint: Name each package so the driver sees it on the load sheet (for example A, legs, 3).
setup.warehouseBoardHint: Where this output is stored after the stage.
setup.warehouseAutomaticHint: Use the default warehouse for this inventory type.
setup.outputNameMissing: Name the output in stage setup
setup.expectedPiecesHint: Soft target for the floor — workers can add more or fewer pieces while working.
setup.consumeInputs: Uses these pieces from earlier stages
setup.consumeInputsHint: Each semi-finished piece can be taken by only one stage — once claimed, it moves up the chain.
setup.takeSemiUnavailableHint: This is at the start of the flow — configure later stages to take work from stages that produce before them.
setup.takeSemiAllClaimedHint: Another stage already takes those semi-finished pieces. Unassign them there first, or take the next piece that stage makes.
setup.noUpstream: No saved components to use yet — name outputs on earlier stages first.
setup.bomEmpty: No materials on this product yet.
setup.rawMaterialsHint: Pick only what this stage needs — for example fabric on upholstery, not on carpentry.
setup.materialsBoardHint: Assign how much of each product material this stage uses. What’s fully claimed here won’t appear on other stages.
setup.materialsBoardBomEmpty: Add materials on the product BOM first.
setup.materialsBoardPoolEmpty: No materials left to assign — other stages already claimed the full BOM qty.
setup.takesInSemiOnlyHint: Receive semi-finished pieces from earlier stages.

MATERIAL_PREP.heading: Prepare materials for: {productLine}.
MATERIAL_PREP.l1: Pull fabric, wood, foam, and hardware per the bill of materials.
MATERIAL_PREP.l2: Label kits for carpentry, painting, and upholstery.
MATERIAL_PREP.l3: Flag shortages to purchasing before releasing the kit.

CARPENTRY.heading: Carpentry for: {productLine}.
CARPENTRY.l1: Cut and assemble frames to drawing dimensions.
CARPENTRY.l2: Sand all visible surfaces; check joints and squareness.
CARPENTRY.l3: Stage completed frames for painting / upholstery.

PAINTING.heading: Finishing / paint for: {productLine}.
PAINTING.l1: Apply primer and finish coats per color reference.
PAINTING.l2: Allow full cure time before handing off to assembly.
PAINTING.l3: Protect finished surfaces for transport to next stage.

FOAM.heading: Foam for: {productLine}.
FOAM.l1: Cut and shape foam to the approved pattern and density.
FOAM.l2: Check thickness and fit against the frame before covering.

UPHOLSTERY.heading: Upholstery for: {productLine}.
UPHOLSTERY.l1: Cut fabric to pattern; match grain and color batch.
UPHOLSTERY.l2: Foam and cover to the approved sample.
UPHOLSTERY.l3: Inspect seams and staples before assembly handoff.

ASSEMBLY.heading: Assemble: {productLine}.
ASSEMBLY.l1: Join carpentry, paint, and upholstery components.
ASSEMBLY.l2: Fit hardware and verify dimensions against the order.
ASSEMBLY.l3: Move complete unit to inspection with paperwork.

INSPECTION.heading: Quality inspection for: {productLine}.
INSPECTION.l1: Run the stage checklist; photograph defects if any.
INSPECTION.l2: Pass only if dimensions, finish, and fabric match the order.
INSPECTION.l3: Fail with clear rework notes for the owning stage.

PACKAGING.heading: Package: {productLine}.
PACKAGING.l1: Wrap and crate for safe transport; add corner protection.
PACKAGING.l2: Attach packing list and factory order label.
PACKAGING.l3: Stage for delivery only after QC pass.

DELIVERY.heading: Deliver: {productLine}.
DELIVERY.l1: Confirm address, window, and contact on the sales order.
DELIVERY.l2: Collect POD signature / photo on delivery.

DEFAULT.l1: Follow the shop drawing and order specifications.
DEFAULT.l2: Update task progress and attach required photos before complete.
